subtopics.title: The Three Weather Systems in One Sweep

questions.question: Which ingredient does a tropical cyclone need that a mid-latitude cyclone does not?
options: An ocean surface warmer than about 26,5 degrees Celsius as its energy source
The Coriolis force
A centre of low pressure
Air rising at its core

questions.question: No tropical cyclone can ever be born on the equator because:
options: The equatorial ocean is always too cold
The Coriolis force is zero there, so the storm has no spin to borrow
The trade winds converge there
There is too little moisture at the equator

questions.question: The quickest single clue on a synoptic map that a low south of the country is a mid-latitude cyclone and not a tropical cyclone is:
options: Its widely spaced isobars
The letter H at its centre
The fronts trailing from the low
The fact that it lies over land

questions.question: A developing tropical system receives its name at which stage of its growth?
options: At the tropical disturbance stage
Only once its eye becomes visible
Only when it makes landfall
At the tropical storm stage, before it becomes a full tropical cyclone

subtopics.title: Anticyclones, Travelling Disturbances and Local Climates

questions.question: A Highveld July is dry, frosty and endlessly sunny mainly because:
options: The Kalahari High sits over the plateau and its inversion caps the interior
Cold fronts strengthen over the interior in winter
The moisture front moves inland in winter
The urban heat island blocks rising air

questions.question: A berg wind arrives at the coast hot and dry because the air:
options: Blows in from the warm Mozambique Channel
Was heated by fires on the plateau
Descends from the plateau and warms by compression on the way down
Crosses the cold Benguela current

questions.question: On a calm, clear winter night, the mildest place in a valley is:
options: The valley floor beside the river
The exposed crest of the ridge
The frost pocket
The thermal belt partway up the slope

questions.question: Which measure directly reduces the urban heat island effect?
options: Expanding tarred parking areas
Planting parks, street trees and green roofs across the city
Removing wind corridors between buildings
Encouraging more private car commuting

questions.question: The Orange River flows all year and crosses arid country after rising in a wet mountain region. It is therefore classified as:
options: Episodic and deranged
Permanent and exotic
Periodic and misfit
Braided and graded

questions.question: Tributaries joining the main stream at right angles across folded belts of alternating hard and soft rock produce which drainage pattern?
options: Dendritic
Radial
Trellis
Centripetal

questions.question: Drainage density is highest where:
options: Rock is impermeable, slopes are steep and vegetation is sparse
Rainfall is gentle and infiltration is high
The rock is porous sandstone
Dense forest covers the basin

questions.question: A graded river is best described as one that:
options: Flows only during the wet season
Is interrupted by many waterfalls and knickpoints
Has lost its headwaters to a stronger neighbour
Has just enough energy to carry its load, giving a smooth concave longitudinal profile

subtopics.title: Fluvial Landforms, Rejuvenation and Catchment Management

questions.question: On a meander bend, the fastest current and the active undercutting are found:
options: Along the inner slip-off slope
On the outer bank of the bend
In the exact centre of the channel
On the floodplain beyond the banks

questions.question: Which trio of features proves that a river has been rejuvenated?
options: Delta, levee and braided channel
Oxbow lake, slip-off slope and floodplain
Knickpoint, paired terraces and incised meanders
Elbow of capture, wind gap and misfit stream

questions.question: After river capture, the beheaded river typically continues as:
options: A misfit stream, far too small for the valley it occupies
A braided channel
An exotic river
A higher-order stream than before

questions.question: Eutrophication in a stressed river system such as the Vaal is driven by:
options: Clearing invasive alien trees from the catchment
Cold mountain water entering the system
Building fish ladders at weirs
Nutrient enrichment from sewage and fertiliser run-off feeding algal blooms

questions.question: In the three-characters picture, the quiet giant that sits and squashes is:
options: The coastal low
The anticyclone, with its sinking, warming, drying air
The mid-latitude cyclone
The moisture front

questions.question: The summer bully from the warm sea starves within days when it:
options: Reaches the open ocean
Meets the polar front
Moves over land or cool water and loses its warm-water fuel
Crosses into the trade-wind belt

questions.question: The hot, dry, fire-fanning wind of the coastal winter is:
options: The berg wind, plateau air compressed and heated on its way down to the coast
The anabatic breeze rising up the valley sides
The south-westerly that follows a cold front
The trade wind off the Indian Ocean

subtopics.title: A River's Whole Life in One Walk

questions.question: The infant stage of the river — loud, furious, cutting straight down — matches which valley form?
options: A broad silt floodplain
A delta at the coast
An abandoned oxbow loop
A sharp V-shaped valley stepped with rapids and waterfalls

questions.question: An oxbow lake is best described as:
options: A meander loop abandoned when a flood cut through the neck of the bend
A dam built across the main channel
A lake scoured out by ice
The river's mountain source

questions.question: A deep rocky gorge that winds like a meander is evidence that:
options: The valley was cut by wind erosion
An old wandering river was rejuvenated and sliced its curves down into rock
A delta once filled the valley
The river has always been in its infant stage

questions.question: The wind gap left behind after river capture is:
options: The confluence of the two rivers
The undercut outer bank of a meander
The dry notch in the ridge where the beheaded river once flowed
A break in a levee during flood

subtopics.title: The Marks You Can Bank Tonight

questions.question: In this session's practice set, an eight-mark paragraph task is built as:
options: Eight bullet points at one mark each
Two ideas at four marks each in point form
One long definition
Four linked ideas at two marks each, written in full sentences

questions.question: Around a low-pressure cell in the Southern Hemisphere, air circulates:
options: Clockwise
Anticlockwise
Straight inward without turning
Clockwise in summer and anticlockwise in winter

questions.question: Why should every drainage pattern be revised together with its two-word rock clue?
options: Because a pattern named without the rock structure that causes it is only half an answer
Because pattern names change from year to year
Because rock types cannot be identified on maps
Because only three patterns ever appear in questions
